window-restore.context: Two overlapping windows offset diagonally, the front one with a title bar. Used for the restore down button in a window's title bar and for returning a maximised window to its earlier size.

window-cascade.context: Three windows stacked diagonally from the top left to the bottom right. Used for a cascade windows command that arranges open windows in an overlapping staircase.

window-tile.context: A screen divided into four equal windows, each with its own title bar. Used for tiling or arranging open windows in a grid and for four up split screen layouts.

window-snap.context: A window snapped to the left half of the screen beside a dashed empty slot waiting for a second window. Used for snap layouts, docking a window to one side and split screen multitasking.

pop-out-window.context: A window with an arrow leaving it toward a second, smaller detached window. Used for pop out, undock and open in a separate window actions in chat, video and editor apps.

virtual-desktops.context: Three screens in a row with the middle one active, above a bar. Used for virtual desktops, workspaces, spaces and task view features that switch between sets of windows.

show-desktop.context: A monitor with an empty screen and two windows minimised to its bottom edge. Used for show desktop, minimise all and peek at desktop commands.

status-bar.context: The top of a phone screen with the time at the left and a battery at the right, above the rest of the screen. Used for the mobile status bar, system indicators and notification area settings.

system-tray.context: The corner of a taskbar with an up caret that opens a small tray of hidden status icons. Used for the notification area, system tray settings and background apps.

toolbar.context: A horizontal bar holding a row of tool buttons with the first one selected. Used for editor toolbars, action bars and customise toolbar settings.

floating-toolbar.context: A small pill of tools hovering above lines of text. Used for inline formatting bars that appear over selected text and for context toolbars in editors.

ribbon-toolbar.context: A toolbar panel with tabs on top and groups of large and small buttons below split by a divider. Used for ribbon interfaces in office and design apps.

tool-palette.context: A tall narrow strip of tool buttons with the top one selected. Used for tool panels in drawing, photo and design apps.

inspector-panel.context: A window with a right hand panel of label and value rows beside an empty canvas. Used for properties inspectors, attribute panels and detail panes in design and development tools.

scrollbar.context: A scroll track with arrow buttons at both ends and a thumb near the top. Used for scrolling settings, overflow content and scroll behaviour options.

tab-group.context: A row of browser tabs where the first two are joined into a group with a bar beneath them. Used for tab groups, grouped tabs and organising open pages in a browser.

address-bar.context: A long rounded field with a small padlock at the left followed by a web address. Used for the browser address bar, secure connection details and entering a web address.

bookmarks-bar.context: A browser window with a strip of small bookmark ribbons under its top bar. Used for showing or hiding the bookmarks bar and managing saved links.

quick-settings-panel.context: A panel of round quick toggles with some switched on and some off. Used for quick settings, control centre and notification shade panels on phones and computers.

system-nav-buttons.context: A bar holding a back triangle, a home circle and a recent apps square. Used for three button navigation settings and on screen system keys on phones and tablets.

app-icon.context: A rounded app tile with a star in the middle. Used for app icons, application shortcuts, featured apps and changing an app's icon.

app-folder.context: A rounded tile holding four small app tiles. Used for app folders on a home screen, grouped apps and app libraries.

wallpaper-screen.context: A phone whose screen shows a landscape of mountains and a sun. Used for wallpaper, background and lock screen image settings.

multiple-displays.context: Two monitors side by side with the right one smaller. Used for display settings, extending or duplicating a desktop across screens and multi monitor setups.

theater-mode.context: A very wide video frame with a play button and a progress bar beneath it. Used for theatre mode and wide player views on video sites.

layout-hero.context: A page with a large banner block across the top and lines of text below it. Used for hero sections, page headers and landing page templates in site builders.

layout-holy-grail.context: A page layout with a header, a footer and a middle band split into a left rail, main content and a right rail. Used for classic three column web page templates.

layout-bento.context: A bento grid of uneven cells with one large tile, one tall tile and two small tiles. Used for bento style feature grids, dashboards and portfolio layouts.

layout-feed.context: A column of post cards, each with a round avatar and lines of text. Used for social feeds, activity streams and timeline layouts.

layout-centered.context: A page with a narrow column of text centred between wide empty margins. Used for single column article and blog layouts with a comfortable reading width.

layout-magazine.context: A page with a headline across the top, a big image at the left and short text columns at the right. Used for magazine, editorial and news article layouts.

layout-master-detail.context: A window split into a narrow list of rows at the left and a large detail pane at the right. Used for master detail and list detail views in mail, notes and file apps.

layout-pricing-tiers.context: Three pricing cards side by side with the middle one taller and highlighted. Used for pricing tables, plan comparison pages and subscription tiers.

layout-profile-header.context: A page with a wide cover strip and a round avatar overlapping its lower edge above lines of text. Used for profile pages, account headers and social profiles.

layout-sidebar-both.context: A page layout with narrow panels at both the left and right edges around a wide centre. Used for app layouts with navigation on one side and an inspector on the other.

layout-split-hero.context: A banner split in two with text lines and a button at the left and a picture at the right. Used for split hero sections on landing pages and marketing sites.

layout-grid-sidebar.context: A window with a narrow sidebar at the left and a two by two grid of tiles in the main area. Used for galleries, file browsers, catalogues and dashboards.

column-guides.context: A frame filled with tall column bars separated by equal gutters. Used for column grids and layout guides in design and publishing tools.

icon-keylines.context: A square template with a circle and diagonal guide lines crossing it. Used for icon design grids, keyline shapes and pixel grid templates.

safe-area.context: A phone with corner marks inset from its rounded corners and top notch, marking the area that stays clear. Used for safe area insets, screen cutouts and mobile layout guides.

breakpoint-ruler.context: A ruler with three markers above it at different widths. Used for responsive design breakpoints, media queries and viewport width settings.

golden-ratio-grid.context: A rectangle divided into shrinking squares with a spiral curling through them. Used for composition guides, golden ratio overlays and design proportion tools.

cascading-menu.context: A menu list with one row open and a submenu opening beside it. Used for nested menus, flyout submenus and multi level context menus.

radial-menu.context: A round menu split into four segments around a centre dot, with one segment picked. Used for pie menus and radial menus in games, drawing apps and touch interfaces.

navigation-rail.context: A window with a narrow bar of icon buttons down its left edge. Used for navigation rails, activity bars and compact side navigation in apps.

navigation-drawer.context: A phone with a menu panel slid in from the left over part of the screen. Used for navigation drawers, side menus and off canvas menus in mobile apps.

bottom-sheet.context: A phone with a rounded sheet risen from the bottom edge and a grab bar on top. Used for bottom sheets, slide up panels and mobile modal drawers.

action-sheet.context: A group of stacked option buttons above a separate cancel button. Used for action sheets, share sheets and option menus that slide up on phones.

segmented-control.context: A pill divided into three segments with the first one selected. Used for segmented controls, button groups and switching between views.

infinite-scroll.context: List rows fading out above an infinity sign. Used for infinite scrolling, endless feeds and lazy loading settings.

load-more.context: List rows above a wide button holding three dots. Used for load more and show more buttons at the end of lists and search results.

pull-refresh-gesture.context: A phone with its list pulled down and a curved refresh arrow in the gap at the top. Used for pull to refresh gestures that reload a feed or list.

list-swipe-actions.context: A list row slid sideways to reveal two action buttons at its end. Used for swipe actions such as delete, archive and flag in mobile lists.

reorder-list.context: List rows with grip handles, the middle one lifted out of line so it can be moved. Used for drag and drop reordering and sortable lists.

reading-progress.context: A page with a progress bar across its top, two thirds filled. Used for reading progress indicators and scroll progress bars on articles.

focus-ring.context: A button surrounded by an offset outline ring with a gap between them. Used for keyboard focus indicators, focus visible styles and accessibility settings.

skip-to-content.context: A page with a small button in its header and an arrow jumping down past the header to the content. Used for skip links that let keyboard users bypass navigation.

tab-bar-mobile.context: A phone with a bottom tab bar of icon buttons, the first one selected. Used for bottom navigation and tab bars in mobile apps.

confirmation-dialog.context: A dialog card with two lines of text and a pair of buttons, one filled. Used for confirm prompts, alerts and are you sure messages before an action.

input-dialog.context: A dialog card with a title, an empty text field and a filled button. Used for prompts that ask for a name, rename dialogs and quick text entry.

coach-mark.context: A dimmed screen with a spotlight on one button and a tooltip pointing at it. Used for coach marks, product tours and onboarding hints that point out features.

notification-banner.context: A screen with a wide notification bar across its top holding a bell and a line of text. Used for in app banners, announcements and alert bars.

push-notification.context: A phone with a notification card near the top showing an app square and a line of text. Used for push notifications, message previews and notification settings.

skeleton-loader.context: A card of placeholder shapes, a circle and thick bars, shown while content loads. Used for skeleton screens and loading states in apps and websites.

splash-screen.context: A phone showing a bold round logo in the middle and loading dots near the bottom. Used for splash screens, launch screens and app start up settings.

onboarding-screens.context: A phone with a picture, a line of text and page dots at the bottom. Used for onboarding flows, welcome screens and intro walkthroughs in apps.

login-form.context: An avatar above a username field and a password field with hidden characters. Used for sign in pages, login forms and account access.

signup-form.context: A form of stacked fields, a tick box with a line of text and a wide filled button. Used for registration pages, create account forms and newsletter sign ups.

consent-banner.context: A screen with a bar across its bottom holding a round cookie and two small buttons. Used for cookie consent banners and privacy notices on websites.

chat-launcher.context: A round floating button holding a speech bubble in the bottom right corner of a page. Used for live chat widgets, support chat and help buttons on websites.
